chunks.text: WASHER GUIDE How to Use the Washer Whirlpool Model (to confirm) Never wash anything dampened with gasoline, dry- cleaning solvents or other flammable fluids. No washer can completely remove oil. Fire or explosion risk. Use only HE (High Efficiency) detergent. Regular detergent makes too many suds and can cause errors, leaks, long cycles and mould.

Do not reach in while the drum is moving. Do not let children play on or in the washer. Do not keep laundry products on top of the washer. Do not plug it into an extension cord or adapter. 1 Sort laundry: darks apart from lights, very dirty items apart from lightly dirty ones. Keep towels away from corduroy and synthetics, which pick up lint.

2 Empty pockets: coins and small items can block the pump. Close zippers, snaps and hooks, tie strings, and turn knits inside out. 3 Load the drum full but not packed tight: the door must close easily. Mix large and small items and avoid washing a single item. Put small items like baby socks in mesh bags (use more than one bag, filled evenly).

4 Close the door by pushing it firmly until the lock clicks. Add detergent and other products 1 Use only detergent marked HE or High Efficiency. Follow the detergent label for how much to use: too much causes suds and leaks.

2 Pull out the dispenser drawer. Put HE detergent (liquid or powder) in the Main Wash compartment (B). Colour- safe bleach or oxi products can go in with it. Do not mix powder and liquid. 3 If you want: liquid chlorine bleach in (C), no more than 2/3 cup (160 mL) and not past MAX. Only liquid chlorine bleach goes here. Measure it with a cup: do not guess.

4 If you want: liquid fabric softener in (D), not past MAX. Do not use fabric softener balls. 5 Push the drawer in slowly and completely so nothing spills. Never pour products straight onto the clothes. A little water left in the drawer after a wash is normal. 1 The control panel. Press POWER to turn the washer on.

2 Push the cycle selector until the light for the cycle you want comes on. Normal (about 1 hr 12 min): everyday cottons, sheets, casual and no-iron clothes. Heavy Duty (about 1 hr 22 min): sturdy, very dirty items like jeans and work clothes. Delicate (about 37 min): sheer fabrics and lingerie, in mesh bags, small loads only.

3 Rinse & Spin: rinse only, or to add fabric softener to a load. Drain & Spin: empties the water and spins. Clean Washer with affresh: the monthly cleaning cycle (see Washer Care), with an empty drum only.

4 Press TEMP to change the wash temperature. Hot: whites and heavy dirt. Warm: bright colours and medium dirt. Cold: colours that run or fade, and light dirt. Follow the care labels. Rinses are always cold.
5 If you want a beep when the wash ends, press and hold CYCLE SIGNAL to turn it on or off. If a button gives a short tone and its light does not come on, that option is not available for that cycle.

6 Press and hold START/PAUSE for about 3 seconds. You will hear the door lock, unlock and lock again: this is normal. If you do not press START/PAUSE within 5 minutes, the washer turns off. From the manufacturer's manual, page 11. 1 The Status lights show what the washer is doing: Wash, Rinse, Spin, then Done. Door Lock means the door cannot be opened.

2 To add an item: while the Add a Garment light is on (about the first 7 minutes), press START/PAUSE once. The door unlocks. Add the item, close the door and hold START/PAUSE for 3 seconds. Not possible on Rinse & Spin, Drain & Spin or Clean Washer. 3 To pause, press START/PAUSE. To continue, press and hold it for 3 seconds.

4 To change the temperature after starting: press START/ PAUSE once, press TEMP, then hold START/PAUSE for 3 seconds. 5 To cancel, press POWER. The door unlocks. If the water is high or hot, the washer drains first. 6 Pauses, clicks, water splashing and some vibration are normal. The washer uses little water, so you may see little water in the drum.

1 When the Done light comes on, the door unlocks. Take the laundry out straight away: metal zippers and buckles can rust and colours can transfer. 2 Check under the rubber seal at the front of the drum for small items. 3 Do not put stained clothes in the dryer: heat can set the stain. Wash them again first.
4 Leave the door slightly open so the drum dries. Open and close the door before you start the next load. Stains (from the manual's stain guide)

1 Ink, grass, tomato: bleach that suits the fabric, Heavy Duty. Coffee, chocolate, mud: bleach that suits the fabric, Warm, Heavy Duty. Blood: bleach that suits the fabric, Cold or Warm, Normal. Collar rings: bleach that suits the fabric, Normal.

2 Make-up and deodorant: Heavy Duty. Dirty motor oil: Warm, Heavy Duty (never wash items soaked in fuel or solvents). Wash stained items soon for best results. STOP AND CONTACT PROPERTY MANAGEMENT Water leaks from the washer, the hoses or the door, or water backs up out of the drain or sink.

The Wash light keeps flashing after you restart (an error code), or the washer will not fill or drain. A burning smell, smoke, or a loud grinding or banging noise. Press POWER and do not use the washer. The washer does not turn on, or the breaker or fuse for it trips again. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
Based on the manufacturer's manual W10307859B (Use & Care Guide) for this Whirlpool front-loading washer. Pictures are taken from that manual. Updated 20 October 2026.

Whirlpool Model (to confirm) Use only HE (High Efficiency) detergent, and measure it. Other detergents leave a film that causes smells. Do not use abrasive cleaners. Wear rubber gloves when cleaning with bleach and follow the bleach label. Do not take any part of the washer apart or try to repair it. 1 Take the laundry out as soon as the wash ends.

2 Leave the door slightly open so the inside can dry. The door seal is tight, so a closed door traps damp air and causes smells. 3 Wipe spills on the outside with a soft damp cloth or sponge, with mild soap and water. Wipe the outside now and then to keep it clean. Clean the washer once a month 1 Take everything out of the drum. Do not put clothes in for this cycle.

2 Put one AFFRESH washer cleaner tablet in the drum (recommended). Or put 2/3 cup (160 mL) of liquid chlorine bleach in the bleach compartment (C). No detergent, and no more bleach than that. 3 Close the door and the drawer. Press POWER, select CLEAN WASHER with affresh, and press and hold START/ PAUSE.

4 For about 3 minutes the drum turns without water and the door unlocks and locks again, while it checks the drum is empty. This is normal. 5 If the Wash light flashes, items were found: press POWER, take them out and start again. 6 Let the cycle finish (about 54 minutes). Then leave the door slightly open so the inside dries.

7 If the washer already smells, use 3 AFFRESH tablets instead of 1, and wipe away any residue after the cycle. Clean the door seal (when you see stains) 1 Take everything out of the drum. Pull back the coloured door seal (A) and check under it for stains and small items.

2 If there are stains: mix 3/4 cup (177 mL) of liquid chlorine bleach in 1 gallon (3.8 L) of warm water. Wipe the seal with a damp cloth and this mix, wait 5 minutes, then wipe it dry. Leave the door open to air dry. Clean the dispenser drawer (when products build up) 1 Pull the drawer out, press the release lever (A) and take the drawer out.

2 Take out the inserts (the siphons in the softener and bleach compartments). Wash all the parts under running water. Do not put them in the dishwasher. 3 Put the inserts back and slide the drawer back in. A clogged softener compartment or drawer stops products from going in. If you go away for a while
1 Use the washer only when you are at home. Before a long trip, leave the door slightly open and ask property management whether the washer should be unplugged and the water taps turned off.

2 If the hot water has not been used for 2 weeks or more, hydrogen gas can build up in the pipes. Before using the washer, turn on all hot water taps and let them run for several minutes. Do not smoke or use any flame while you do this. STOP AND CONTACT PROPERTY MANAGEMENT

A water hose behind the washer is bulging, cracked, kinked or leaking. (The manual says the hoses should be replaced every 5 years.) A bad smell stays after the monthly cleaning cycle. The washer needs to be moved, or the room could freeze: this must be done by a technician. Water leaks from the washer, or the Wash light keeps flashing after you restart.

If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management. Based on the manufacturer's manual W10307859B (Use & Care Guide) for this Whirlpool front-loading washer. Pictures are taken from that manual. Updated 20 October 2026.

WASHER GUIDE Washer Troubleshooting Whirlpool Model (to confirm) Do not open the washer cabinet or try to repair it. If water is leaking near an electrical outlet, do not touch the washer or the plug. Never use an extension cord or adapter, and never remove the ground prong from the plug. The Wash light is flashing (error code)

1 This washer has no screen. A flashing Wash light means an error. Count the flashes before each 2-second pause: for example 8 flashes, pause, 1 flash is code F8 E1. 2 F8 E1, no water: press POWER. Check that both water taps behind the washer (hot and cold) are fully open and the hoses are not kinked. Unplug the washer, plug it back in, choose the cycle and press START/PAUSE.

3 F9 E1, will not drain: press POWER. Unplug the washer, plug it back in, choose the cycle and press START/PAUSE. Pocket items can block the pump. 4 Any other F and E code: press POWER. If there is a lot of water inside, select DRAIN & SPIN first. Then choose the cycle and press START/PAUSE. 5 If any code comes back, stop using the washer and contact property management.
Will not start or will not turn on 1 Close the door firmly, then press and hold START/PAUSE for 3 seconds. 2 After a wash, the door must be opened and closed before a new cycle can start.

3 Buttons do not respond: press POWER twice, then try choosing a cycle again. If the controls are locked, a button held for 3 seconds unlocks them. The manual does not say which button on this model: check with property management. 4 No power at all: check it is plugged in and that the breaker or fuse for the washer has not tripped. Do not use an extension cord.

5 Short pauses of about 2 minutes are normal in some cycles. An overloaded washer may not run: take some items out. 6 Stops at the same point every time: unplug the washer, wait 5 minutes, plug it back in and run another cycle. 1 If the Add a Garment light is on, press START/PAUSE once. The door unlocks.

2 If water is left inside: press START/ PAUSE, select DRAIN & SPIN and hold START/PAUSE for 3 seconds. The door unlocks when the spin ends. Clothes are still wet, or water is left 1 Run DRAIN & SPIN (no detergent). Delicate spins slowly, so clothes come out wetter: choose a cycle with a faster spin.

2 One heavy item or a bulky load can unbalance the drum. Add more items or spread the load out. If still wet, take half the load out and spin again. 3 Too many suds slow the spin. The washer runs a special routine on its own to remove them. Use only HE detergent and less of it next time.

1 Clicks from the door lock, water spraying, short pauses, gurgling or humming while draining, and zippers or buckles touching the drum are normal. Rattling: check under the door seal for coins or small items. From the manufacturer's manual,

2 Shaking: do not wash a single item, do not pack the drum tight, and load evenly. If it still shakes, walks or bangs, contact property management: the washer may not be level. 1 Little water in the drum or few suds: normal for this washer. A little water left in the dispenser is also normal. 2 Drips from the door after you open it during Add a Garment are normal.

3 Water on the floor: too much or non-HE detergent can cause suds that leak from the back. Use only HE detergent and measure it. If it still leaks, stop and contact property management. 4 Hot water feels less hot after many loads in a row: this is normal.

5 The cycle takes longer than expected: the washer adds time for suds, an unbalanced load, a single or bulky item, or a large load on Delicate. This is normal. 1 Products in the wrong place: detergent and colour-safe bleach in Main Wash (B), only liquid chlorine bleach in (C), fabric softener in (D). Measure, pour slowly and wipe spills.

2 Products left in the drawer: clean the drawer and inserts (see Washer Care) and check both water taps are fully open. 1 Bad smell: use only HE detergent, leave the door open between washes, and run CLEAN WASHER every month (3 AFFRESH tablets if it already smells).

2 Lint, residue, grey whites or dull colours: put detergent in the dispenser, not the drum. Sort properly, do not overload, and check pockets for tissue. Use a little more HE detergent for very dirty loads or hard water.

3 Detergent does not dissolve well in cold water below 60°F (15.6°C): use warm or hot if the label allows. Powder may not dissolve on Delicate: use liquid detergent instead. 4 Colour transfer, wrinkles or tangles: take clothes out as soon as the washer stops. For wrinkles, do not overload, use Delicate, or warm water if safe for the fabric.

5 Fabric softener balls do not work in this washer: use the softener compartment. STOP AND CONTACT PROPERTY MANAGEMENT Water leaks from the washer, the hoses or the door, or water backs up out of the drain or sink. The Wash light keeps flashing after you restart (an error code), or the washer will not fill or drain.

A burning smell, smoke, or a loud grinding or banging noise. Press POWER and do not use the washer. The washer does not turn on, or the breaker or fuse for it trips again. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
Based on the manufacturer's manual W10307859B (Use & Care Guide) for this Whirlpool front-loading washer. Pictures are taken from that manual. Updated 20 October 2026.

TROUBLESHOOTING First try the solutions suggested here or visit our website and reference FAQs (Frequently Asked Questions) to possibly avoid the cost of a service call... In U.S.A. http://www.whirlpool.com/help - In Canada www.whirlpool.ca Error codes If your Wash Status LED light is flashing: This indicates that there is an issue with your washer.

To determine your error code: First, notice the sequence of the flashes. The wash status light will flash on for .5 seconds, then off for .5 seconds, followed by a pause of 2 seconds and repeat. Count the number of flashes before the pause to determine your first error code (F code). You will then see a pause of 2 seconds, then start counting again to determine your second code (E code).

Once you have gone through the sequence, you can determine your Error Code. Example: If you have 8 flashes (0.5 sec On, 0.5 sec Off) - pause (2 sec) - 1 flash (0.5 sec On) this represents an "F8E1" error code. If you are still experiencing problems, please call the numbers at the front of the book, or call for service.

Check the list below for potential problem and troubleshooting checks. "F8EI" on display (Long Fill - no water or insufficient water supply) Press POWER to cancel the cycle. Unplug washer or disconnect power. Electrical Shock Hazard Plug into a grounded 3 prong outlet. Do not remove ground prong. Do not use an adapter. Do not use an extension cord. Failure to follow these instructions can result in death, fire, or electrical shock.

Plug in washer or reconnect power. Re-select cycle and press START/PAUSE. If the problem remains, call for service. "F9EI" on display (Drain Problem) Press POWER to cancel the cycle. Unplug washer or disconnect power. Plug in washer or reconnect power. Re-select cycle and press START/PAUSE. If the problem remains, call for service. "F--E--" Variables (Washer

Problem) Press POWER to cancel the cycle. Select DRAIN & SPIN if there is excessive water in the washer. Re-select cycle and press START/PAUSE. If the problem remains, call for service. Noisy, vibrating, off-balance Is the washer level? The washer must be level. The four feet should be properly installed, and the nuts should be tightened against the washer cabinet.

All four feet of the washer must be in firm contact with the floor. If the washer is on a pedestal, the washer must be secured to the pedestal and all four pedestal feet must be in firm contact with the floor. Did you empty pockets? You may be hearing items that are caught under the door seal or basket. Check under the door seal and remove items. Washer making a different noise?

As with any new product, you will hear sounds that you are not accustomed to. You may hear various sounds when the door is locked or unlocked, and during the washing, rinsing, or spinning process. Between changes in wash actions, there will be momentary pauses. You will hear water spraying and splashing during the wash and rinse cycles. These new sounds and pauses are part of normal washer operation.

Is washer installed on a sturdy and solid floor? Refer to the "Installation Instructions" for flooring requirements. Noise and vibration may be reduced by placing a piece of 3/4" (19 mm) plywood underneath your washer. The plywood may extend underneath both washer and dryer to keep them at equal heights. Is the washer gurgling or humming?

As water is drained from the washer, you may hear air being pulled through the pump. This happens during the end of draining. It is normal. Are you washing items with metal snaps, buckles, or zippers? You may hear metal items touching the washer drum. This is normal. Were the 4 shipping bolts in the back of the machine removed? See "Remove Transport System." Leaking Was the door opened during "Add a Garment"?

Water can drip off the inside of the door, when the door is opened after the start of a cycle. Is HE detergent being used? The non-High Efficiency detergents can cause oversudsing which can leak from the rear of the washer. Are the fill hoses tight? Are the fill hose gaskets properly seated? Check both ends of each hose. See "Connect the Inlet Hoses." Is the drain hose properly installed?

The drain hose should be secured to the drainpipe or laundry tub. See "Secure the Drain Hose." Is the sink or drain clogged? Sink and drainpipe must be able to carry away 17 gal. (64 L) of water per minute. If the sink or drain is clogged or slow, water can back up out of drainpipe or sink. Check household plumbing (laundry tubs, faucets, drainpipe, water pipes) for leaks. 19

Dispenser operation Did you follow the manufacturer's directions when adding detergent and fabric softener to the dispensers? Measure detergent and fabric softener. Slowly pour into the dispensers. Wipe up all spills. Dilute fabric softener in the fabric softener dispenser. Did you put powdered or liquid color-safe bleach into the liquid chlorine bleach dispenser (on some models)?

Add powdered or liquid color-safe bleach directly to the washer basket. Do not use the chlorine bleach dispenser for color-safe bleach. Is the fabric softener dispenser clogged? Clean the fabric softener dispenser. See "Washer Care" for details. Are the laundry products in the correct dispenser compartment? Add the correct amounts of detergent, fabric softener, or liquid chlorine bleach to the correct compartments.

Add powdered or liquid color-safe bleach to the Main Wash compartment. Is there water in the dispenser at the end of the cycle? A small amount of water will remain inthe dispenser compartment. This is normal. Washer odor See "Cleaning Your Washer"

Are you using AFFRESH ;° washer cleaner on a regular basis? AFFRESH _ washer cleaner removes and avoids odor-causing residue in all High Efficiency washers. For washers where odor is present, use 3 tablets instead of 1 tablet. After the CLEAN WASHER with AFFRESH TM cycle is complete, wipe away residue if necessary. Are you using HE detergent? Use of non-HE detergent can cause a film residue which can result in odor.

Did you leave the door open after use? This washer has a tight seal to avoid water leaks. To avoid odors leave the door open to allow the washer to dry between uses. Door won't unlock Did all of the water drain out of the washer during the spin? Select DRAIN & SPIN to remove any water remaining in the washer. The washer door will unlock at the end of the drain.

Is the door locked and is the "Add a Garment" light on? Press START/PAUSE once. The door will unlock. Washer won't power up Electrical Shock Hazard Plug into a grounded 3 prong outlet. Do not remove ground prong. Do not use an adapter. Do not use an extension cord. Failure to follow these instructions can result in death, fire, or electrical shock.

Is the power cord plugged into a grounded 3 prong outlet? Plug power cord into a grounded 3 prong outlet. Are you using an extension cord? Do not use an extension cord. Has a household fuse blown, or has a circuit breaker tripped? Check that the washer is plugged into a working outlet, and check for blown fuses. Replace the fuse, or reset the circuit breaker. If the problem continues, call an electrician. Is your voltage low?

Check electrical source or call electrician. Washer cyclewon't start Is the washer door firmly shut? The door must be closed during operation. Has a cycle been selected, but START/PAUSE has not been selected and held for 3 seconds? Press and hold START/PAUSE, for 3 seconds. Was the door open after completion of last cycle? The door must be opened and closed again to start a new cycle. Is the door locked?

If door is locked, run a drain cycle and drain the washer. Control won't accept selections or won't shut off Are the touch pad controls locked? Hold for 3 seconds the button to IocWunlock controls. Are the touch pad buttons not responding? Press POWER on the touch-pad twice. Check the touch-pad/ LED assembly by selecting different cycles and changing the options available to confirm the touch-pad/LED assembly is responding. Washer stops working
Does the washer shut down the same time in the same wash cycle repeatedly? Unplug washer or disconnect power. Wait 5 minutes. Plug in washer or reconnect power. Run another cycle. 20

Washer won't dispense Is the washer level? Check that the washer is level. See "Level Washer." Has the drawer dispensed detergent? Check that the dispenser drawer is not clogged with detergent. Are both the hot and cold water faucets turned on? Check water hose connections to the washer. Check for plugged screen in water source. Check the water supply and the water valve. Washer won't fill Low water pressure at home?

Check if the home has low water pressure, open the water faucets. Are both the hot and cold water faucets turned on? Verify hot and cold valve at the water faucets are fully open. Is the water inlet hose kinked? Straighten the hoses. Check water hose connections to the washer and make sure water supply hoses are not obstructed. Check for plugged screen.

Are the water inlet valve screens clogged? Turn off the water and remove inlet hoses from the washer. Remove any accumulated film or particles. Reinstall hoses, turn on water, and check for leaks. Are you using HE detergent? HE detergent is a low sudsing detergent. This is normal and will not affect cleaning performance. Low water?

This washer uses very little water to provide good cleaning results. You will see little or no water splashing in this washer. This is normal. Washer won't run Is the washer in a normal pause in the cycle? The washer pauses for about 2 minutes during certain cycles. Allow the cycle to continue. Some cycles feature periods of tumbling and soak. Is the washer overloaded? Wash smaller loads. Incorrect water temperature or Wash/Rinse temperature

Are the hot and cold water inlet hoses reversed? See "Connect the Inlet Hoses." Are you washing many loads? As your frequency of loads washed increases, the water temperature may decrease for hot and warm temperatures. This is normal. Not enough water/Not enough suds Low water? This washer uses very little water to provide good cleaning results. You will see little or no water splashing in this washer. This is normal.

Are you using HE detergent? HE detergent is a low sudsing detergent. This is normal and will not affect cleaning performance. Washer continues to fill or drain, cycle seems stuck Is the top of drain hose lower than 30" (760 mm) on washer? The top of the drain hose must be at least 30" (760 mm) above the floor. See "Drain System."

Check that the washer is level. Check if the valve is blocked open. If the valve is blocked open, uncontrolled filling will occur. Does the drain extend into the drain pipe more than 41/2'' (114 mm)? Use the drain form to extend the drain hose the proper length into the drain pipe.

Does the drain hose fit too tightly in the standpipe, or is it taped to the standpipe? The drain hose should be loose yet fit securely. Do not seal the drain hose with tape. The hose needs an air gap. See "Secure the Drain Hose." Washer won't drain or spin, water remains inwasher Is the drain hose clogged, or the end of the drain hose more than 96" (2.4 m) above the floor? See "Installation Requirements."

Does the drain hose fit too tightly in the standpipe, or is it taped to the standpipe? The drain hose should be loose yet fit securely. Do not seal the drain hose with tape. The hose needs an air gap. See "Secure the Drain Hose." Does the drain extend into the drain pipe more than 41/2'' (114 mm)? Use the drain form to extend the drain hose the proper length into the drain pipe. Excessive suds?

When excessive suds are detected, a special suds routine automatically starts. Cycle will complete once extra suds are removed. This will occur more frequently when a non-HE detergent is used. Is the load balanced? A single or bulky item may cause imbalance. Add more items or redistribute the load. Is the drum empty?

Rotate drum by hand to check for any binding of the spin basket. Check for clothing stuck between spin basket and outer tub. Move open end drum up and down while holding outer tub steady and check for looseness (more than 1/4" (6.35 mm) of movement). Is the load balanced? A single or bulky item may cause imbalance. Add more items or redistribute the load. Cycle time changes/Cycle too long Excessive suds?

When excessive suds are detected, a special suds routine automatically starts. This routine will add time to the original cycle. Did the load cause imbalance? When an imbalance occurs, an imbalance routine will start to redistribute the load. This extends the cycle. Are you washing a single item or bulky load? Spin time is added if an unbalanced load is detected. The washer will attempt to redistribute the load with additional tumbling.
Did you wash a large load in a delicate cycle? When using the Delicate wash cycle you should use small loads. This ensures a gentle wash for your garments without increasing cycle times. 21

Load too wet Did you use the right cycle for the load being washed? Select a cycle with a higher spin speed. Did you wash a single item or bulky items or have you overloaded the washer? A single item, bulky items, or overloading may cause imbalance. Add items or try to evenly distribute your wet laundry in the drum, and start a Rinse/Drain & Spin cycle. If the laundry is still wet, take half of the load out of the washer and try again.

Did you use HE detergent? Suds during rinse and spin cycles can reduce spin speed. Use HE detergent. Residue, lint, stains on load; gray whites, dingy colors Did you add detergent to the dispenser? For best results, add detergent to the detergent compartment. Do not add detergent to the washer drum. Did you sort properly? Sort lint givers (towels, chenille) from lint takers (corduroy, synthetics).

Transfer of dye can occur when mixing whites and colors in a load. Sort dark clothes from whites and lights. Did you overload the washer? Do not overload the washer. The washer can be fully loaded, but not tightly packed. The wash load must be balanced. Lint can be trapped in the load if overloaded. Check the following: Was paper or tissue left in pockets? Did you use enough HE detergent?

Follow manufacturer's recommendations for the type of load you are washing. For best performance, use only High Efficiency detergent. Use enough HE detergent to remove soil and hold it in suspension. Do you have hard water? Use more detergent for washing heavy soils in cold or hard water. Is your water colder than 60°F (15.6°0)? Wash water colder than 60°F (15.6°C) may not completely dissolve the detergent.

Use hot or warm washes if safe for the fabric load. Make sure your hot water system is adequate to provide a hot water wash. Are you using a low speed wash cycle? Powdered detergents may not dissolve well in a slow-speed cycle. For best results, use liquid detergent for slow-speed cycles such as Delicate. Did you unload the washer promptly? To avoid transfer of dye, unload the washer as soon as it stops.

Did you use a fabric softener dispensing ball? Dispensing balls will not operate correctly with this washer. Add liquid fabric softener to the fabric softener compartment. Did you use powdered detergent in a low-speed cycle? Consider using liquid detergent. Load is wrinkled, twisted, tangled Did you unload the washer promptly? Unload the washer as soon as it stops. Did you use the right cycle for the load being washed?

Use the Delicate cycle with a low spin speed to reduce wrinkling. Did you overload the washer? The wash load must be balanced and not overloaded. Loads should tumble freely during washing. Was the wash water warm enough to relax wrinkles? If safe for load, use warm or hot wash water. Are the hot and cold water hoses reversed?
Check that the hot and cold water hoses are connected to the right faucets. A hot rinse followed by spin will cause wrinkling. See "Connect the Inlet Hoses." 22
